# Preloading shows on the page: the next view is ready before the click

## Context

`examples/preloadingAssets` shows the service worker preloading assets. It has no catalog record and was last changed in July 2025. #21140's target renews it as "Ready before the click, and offline", and the band's epic #21358 counts it among its nine renewals. No leaf was filed.

## The Problem

The band's read ([its rows](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21142#issuecomment-6980292611)): "Two tabs with a portrait each. The preload happens three seconds after load, and only the console says so." A visitor cannot see that anything was preloaded, or that it came from a cache.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/worker/ServiceBase.mjs`: the service worker base the example builds on.
- `examples/preloadingAssets`: the folder to rebuild in place.
- Whether the example can run offline in a production build on `dev` is not verified. The target itself says the leaf verifies that first.

## The Fix

Step one is a check: build the example for production, load it, take the network away, and record on this ticket whether it still runs. Then rebuild in place. The next view preloads when the pointer rests on its tab or button, a counter on the page shows what came from the cache and what from the network, and one line says what to try. If step one passed, a switch on the page takes the network away and the example keeps working. If it failed, the example ships without that switch, its caption makes no offline claim, and the gap gets its own engine ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The result of the offline check in a production build is on this ticket before the rebuild starts.
- [ ] The preload is triggered by the visitor's own hover, and the page shows what was served from the cache.
- [ ] One line on the first frame names the action.
- [ ] The caption claims offline only if the check passed and the page has the switch.
- [ ] No console error, at 1440×900 and at 390×844, in every theme its sibling examples offer.
- [ ] A record in Workers & Platform with a cover from its first frame (through `neomjs/pages`).
- [ ] The look: the first frame and the frame after a preloaded switch, both sizes, Neo Dark, on the pull request, read cold by the reviewer's seat.

**Publication (added 22 Nov, the same for every leaf of this wave).** The criterion above that names this example's record, card, tile or cover in the catalog is met in one of two ways. If #21856 (one catalog file per group) has merged before this leaf's pull request, the pull request carries the record in its group's file. If not, the pull request merges without it: the record stands as text in the pull request body, the cover is merged on `neomjs/pages`, and the catalog entry lands with #21934, the wave's publication pass. Either way this leaf closes with its example.

## Out of Scope

Changes to the service worker's caching strategy. A general offline mode for the Portal.

## Avoided Traps

- **An offline claim from dev mode.** The service worker behaves differently there; the check runs on a production build.
- **A timer that preloads.** Three seconds after load proves nothing to a visitor; the preload follows their hover.

### @neo-gpt-sophie - 2026-11-22T19:23:23Z

**Production offline preflight passed.** I built the existing example with `npm run build-all -- --env prod --npminstall no --parsedocs no`. The checked-out topic branch and `dev` at `dac56c19b6f4` have identical preload-demo and Service Worker sources. Chromium ran the resulting `mws81c68` build.

The packaged Service Worker cached Alice’s image while Bob was selected. I waited for the actual CacheStorage entry, disabled the browser context’s network, and verified an uncached request failed. On the first Alice click, the image came from the Service Worker with HTTP 200 and decoded at its full 128 px width. The warmed shell also reloaded offline. In a fresh control I disabled the ordinary HTTP cache and removed only Alice’s CacheStorage entry. The image then failed offline and recovered when the network returned.

I’ll keep the cache and network counters tied to the path that loaded each asset. The demo switch will send its own asset requests through cache only, so visitors can reproduce the tab switch without opening browser developer tools. The Service Worker’s shared policy stays in `src/worker/ServiceBase.mjs`.
